findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 8dfbf8a57d0a02539e9adfb3de6cdd5cff99e20abeb9308f53a2a2845c063119; all 8 declared sources passed current access review.

Claims remain bounded to the public-record scope of Texas Comptroller and Secretary of State pages, the FTC practice of independently locating contact information, and the Texas Attorney General page’s record-preservation fields. No source is converted into authentication, authority, legitimacy, reputation, fairness, fraud, value, legal effect, contract, or transaction advice.

The article invents no real owner, sender, entity, representative, address, phone, domain, source result, offer, property, contract, transaction, price, testimonial, success rate, or owner-specific legal, tax, accounting, title, appraisal, investment, or transaction conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Comptroller, Comptroller’s Databases (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Comptroller database directory identifies the Taxable Entity Search and the recorded right-to-transact-business status available from Comptroller records.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the result only as one public-record column at query time; it does not treat a status result as authentication of a person, offer, authority, reputation, or transaction.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Comptroller, Franchise Tax Account Status (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Comptroller account-status instructions describe the scope of franchise-tax account-status searches and certificates.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article records only what the selected status source displays and does not infer representative authority, offer authenticity, buyer quality, legal effect, or a transaction decision.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Secretary of State, Let’s Do Business (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Secretary of State page describes business-organization filings and public-record services.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article treats those records as entity-record evidence only and does not claim that a filing authenticates the contacting person or approves an offer.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Secretary of State, Filing Options (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Secretary of State filing-options page identifies available filing and record-request channels.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article mentions the official channel only as a way to locate entity-record evidence and makes no claim about record sufficiency, authority, legitimacy, or offer quality.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Secretary of State, Business Organization FAQs (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Secretary of State business-organization FAQs explain the limited public-record role of the office and identify record questions owners may research.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article preserves that limited scope and does not convert a record match into proof of a sender’s identity, authority, reputation, or transaction legitimacy.

sources_inspected.label: Federal Trade Commission, Business Impersonator Scams (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The FTC business-impersonator guidance supports contacting a business through independently located contact information rather than relying only on an unexpected message.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that practice only to create an independent-contact comparison column and does not label a mismatch as impersonation or fraud.

sources_inspected.label: Federal Trade Commission, Online Search Results: The Good, the Bad, and the Scammy (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The FTC alert warns that some search results and sponsored listings can lead to impostor contact information.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article therefore asks owners to record how independent contact details were located and does not treat the first search result as verified evidence.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Attorney General, File a Consumer Complaint (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Attorney General complaint page identifies business and contact details that may be preserved with a consumer record.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article borrows only the record-preservation fields; it does not say a mismatch warrants a complaint or treat a complaint number as a merits decision.
